title: How We Built Snappr Pro for Our Customers
summary: We interviewed nine clients who book corporate business photography, then built Snappr Pro from what they asked for. Every feature, and who asked.
body_markdown:
## The feedback we heard in every single interview


Our design and engineering leads sat down with some of our customers and asked one blunt question: what do you find great about working with us and what can we improve?


The answers were more specific than we expected. A dental group with offices across eight states told us their team was having trouble managing access and coordinating with photographers. An event agency with multiple planners were struggling with managing dozens of galleries.


Different industries, different volumes, the same underlying problem. Everyone in the room was booking photoshoots at real scale, and none of them were doing it on tooling built for that. These were not businesses that needed better photos. They were businesses that had outgrown the way they were capturing photos.


That gap is not unique to us. Content Marketing Institute's B2B research found that 45% of organizations lack a scalable model for content creation and 54% name lack of resources as a top challenge. The same research found that among companies with dedicated content teams, 54% run those teams with just two to five people. Small teams, growing visual demands, tooling built for one person.


So we built Snappr Pro with features to fill those gaps.


## Room for the whole team


More users under one account. This was the most common request.


‍


Pay-as-you-go gives you one account because, for most bookings, one person owns the whole job end to end. These customers had grown past that. A dental group had several people booking across their offices. A venture firm had brought in a contractor to migrate photo files. A funeral-home marketing agency had a bookkeeper pulling invoices. An agency's video editor was downloading footage for edit. In every case, our customers' teams were forming around the account and they needed a way to collaborate more easily.


‍


One customer described bookings landing under her name but carrying a colleague's phone number, so the photographer called the wrong person. Separate logins fix who owns what, not just who can get in.


‍


Snappr Pro includes a team workspace for multiple users, each with their own login, and a shared history so every booking and gallery sits in one place regardless of who created it.


## No more rewriting briefs every time


60% of the accounts we spoke with had built something genuinely good and were rebuilding it every month. Write out what you want. Send it to the rep. The rep forwards it to the photographer. Do it again next time.


‍


One customer had refined his down to an itemized list precise enough that he described the process as copy, paste, copy, paste. An event manager was producing a one-page manifest per booking covering room locations, floors, walking directions and shot timing. An agency owner had a template with a four-hour timeline, a b-roll checklist and a per-video script list. These were teams who knew exactly what they wanted. They just had nowhere to keep it.


‍


Pro gives them a place. Creative guidelines live on your account, and attach to shoots automatically so the photographer arrives already knowing your style preferences, your must-have shots and your logistics notes.


‍


## A roster of photographers you trust


Some accounts asked to save preferred photographers. Some asked for the ability to rule someone out.


‍


The reason was never about micromanagement. It was about compounding a good match. A multifamily developer explained that rebooking a photographer she had worked with before saved her a site visit: he already knew the team, he already had access, nothing needed re-explaining. An event agency wanted the same photographer across a multi-day conference because clients recognize him by day two and relax on camera. Every repeat booking with the right creator is worth more than the first one.


‍


Pro adds favorite photographer management, so you can build that roster deliberately rather than by luck, and set aside creators who were not the right fit for your work.


‍


## A gallery you can search


A few accounts asked for search across their whole image history. Both had reached the point where they owned enough photography for that to be a real question. One of them was working out of our portal in preference to her own company's internal database, purely because it was easier to navigate.


‍


Pro adds smart image search across your gallery. Search a term like team portrait and get matching images from every booking you have ever made, not just the shoot you happen to have open.


‍


A photo you can find is a photo you can publish, and a growing library is only an asset if you can find what you need from it. Our guide to why[professional photography is essential for every business](https://www.snappr.com/blog/why-professional-photography-is-essential-for-every-business-11-powerful-reasons) covers the downstream revenue case in more detail.


‍

Pro is for teams booking shoots regularly enough that pay-as-you-go has started to chafe, but who are not ready for an enterprise contract. It covers the same multi-location brands, in-house and independent agencies, event and marketing teams, ecommerce, real estate, automotive marketplaces, and more.


It is not for enterprise-scale businesses. If you need API access, custom workflows, unlimited seats or bespoke integrations, that conversation is still[Snappr for Enterprise](https://www.snappr.com/enterprise) . Pro is the tier that was missing underneath it.

## Frequently asked questions


### What is included in Snappr Pro?


[Snappr Pro](https://www.snappr.com/pro) is an annual membership that adds a three-seat team workspace, saved creative guidelines, favorite and blocked photographer management, and smart image search across your gallery. It also reduces the service fee on every booking from 15% to 9%.


### How much does Snappr Pro cost?


[Pro is $49 for the first year](https://www.snappr.com/pro) at launch pricing, down from the standard $99. It is billed as a single annual payment, auto-renews, and can be cancelled at any time. There is no spend commitment attached.


### How is Pro different from pay-as-you-go?


Pay-as-you-go gives you one login and the standard 15% service fee. Pro is built for teams: multiple seats with separate logins, shared booking history, reusable shoot guidelines, photographer preferences that persist between bookings, and a lower fee per shoot.


### When does a Snappr Pro membership pay for itself?


Because the membership cuts the service fee by six percentage points, it typically covers its own cost within the first handful of bookings at launch pricing. Teams booking monthly or more usually clear the $49 well inside the first quarter.


### Should I choose Pro or Snappr Enterprise?


Choose[Pro](https://www.snappr.com/pro) if you need a few seats, consistent shoot guidelines and a better rate without a spend commitment. Choose[Snappr Enterprise](https://www.snappr.com/enterprise) if you need API access, custom workflow automation, unlimited users or bespoke integrations, which come with an annual contract and a dedicated account manager.
